title: John 21: not every deed is written — enough is written for saving knowledge of Christ
source_text: VI. Quod attinet ad alterum locum, ubi Joannes affirmat non omnia fuisse scripta quae fecit Christus, neque mundum capere posse libros qui de iis scribi possent, respondeo neque nos dicere omnia Christi facta scripta fuisse: sed solummodo totam ejus doctrinam, quantum ad salutem sufficit. De gestis vero Christi tantum scriptum est, quantum satis est ut Christum possimus cognoscere, & per notitiam ejus ad vitam aeternam pervenire, ut docet idem Joannes cap. 20. Multa, inquit, alia signa edidit Jesus in conspectu discipulorum suorum quae non sunt scripta in hoc libro. Haec autem scripta sunt ut credatis Jesum esse Christum Dei filium, & ut credentes, vitam habeatis per nomen ejus.
pass_a_gloss: As for the other place, where John affirms that not all things were written which Christ did, nor that the world could contain the books that could be written about them, I answer that neither do we say that all the deeds of Christ were written: but only his whole doctrine, as much as suffices for salvation. But concerning the deeds of Christ only so much is written as is enough that we may know Christ, and through the knowledge of him arrive at eternal life, as the same John teaches in chapter 20. Many other signs, he says, Jesus performed in the sight of his disciples which are not written in this book. But these are written that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ the Son of God, and that believing you may have life through his name.
pass_b_english: We never claimed every deed of Jesus is in the book.
What is claimed: the whole doctrine needful for salvation is written.
John 20 sets the measure: enough signs for knowing Christ unto life.
Unwritten deeds do not open a second equal rule beside Scripture.
